summary: Build EHR, FHIR, and digital health skills in 5 days. Learn practical governance, analytics, and reporting for healthcare teams.
lede: Health informatics courses help professionals who manage, analyze, govern, or implement digital health systems make information useful in care delivery. They cover EHR data quality and clinical coding, mapping HL7 FHIR information exchange, and setting governance and security processes for health records. Learners also practice evaluating clinical decision support, shaping health dashboards and KPIs, and planning digital health implementation around service needs.
audienceIntro: This advanced course is designed for professionals who manage, analyze, govern, or implement digital health systems and need practical control over informatics workflows.
audience: Population Health Informatics Specialists using registry
prerequisites: Recommended prerequisites include working knowledge of healthcare operations, clinical or administrative information workflows, and basic data handling in spreadsheets or reporting tools. Prior exposure to EHRs, HL7 concepts, or data governance is helpful but not mandatory for completion of the course. Participants should bring a laptop for practical exercises. Coding is not required for completion, although advanced concepts such as interoperability architecture, AI-assisted documentation, and analytics workflows will be taught at an operational and conceptual level rather than as production engineering.
